propositions: Context-limit escalation on provider-qualified runs (e.g. Bedrock) silently substitutes bare Anthropic model ids, bypassing the model-class table and causing provider-crossing failures or unbudgeted spend.

The _rung_target function derives escalation targets from ladder constants alone without considering the run's primary model, causing provider-qualified models to degrade to bare Anthropic family names.
A Bedrock-qualified primary with no configured class table escalates to bare Anthropic ids like claude-opus-4-8, leaving cfg.model_provider untouched and composing invalid Bedrock model ids.
The one-criterion retry executes on common substitution before rare deep escalation, not confined to edge cases as intended.

The fix threads the run's primary model into _rung_target and compares providers: if they differ on higher rungs, the rung is dropped rather than crossed; if they differ on the primary's own rung, the primary is returned verbatim.
